objective: Yahoo public HackerOne deep hunt — find and prove unusual bugs, in-scope only (*.yahoo.com, *.aol.com, *.techcrunch.com), throttled, manual-style

observations.text: crt.sh mapped 4726 unique subdomains: yahoo.com 1482, aol.com 3171, techcrunch.com 75
sandbox DNS proxy REFUSES CNAME queries — takeover detection must be HTTP-fingerprint based, not DNS based
sweep done: 4 of 300 legacy hosts answer; rest are dark

assumptions.believes: Yahoo's main properties are well-hardened by a mature security team
assumptions.enforcement: HackerOne triage history; bug bounty since 2013
assumptions.violated_if: we find a remotely triggerable flaw on a core property

assumptions.believes: Legacy/acquired subdomains (aol.com, oath-era) may point at decommissioned infra
assumptions.violated_if: a dangling CNAME to a claimable service is found

hypotheses.statement: A Yahoo/AOL API subdomain reflects an arbitrary Origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials:true, enabling cross-origin theft of authenticated responses
hypotheses.attacker_view: attacker site makes credentialed fetch() to api endpoint; browser allows read if ACAO echoes evil.com + ACAC true
hypotheses.defender_view: Yahoo uses a strict allowlist of origins on API endpoints; main properties hardened

hypotheses.statement: develop.techcrunch.com (WordPress) discloses usernames via REST API /wp-json/wp/v2/users or ?author=N redirects, enabling targeted credential attacks
hypotheses.attacker_view: enumerate valid WP usernames from the dev site, then use in password-spray or social engineering
hypotheses.defender_view: WP REST user endpoint disabled or requires auth; author archives disabled

hypotheses.statement: The rejection may be channel-specific; the same assumption may fail on a sibling endpoint.
hypotheses.investigator_test: Map sibling endpoints sharing the object and test the cheapest one.

hypotheses.statement: api.qa.cmi.aol.com (AWS API Gateway, 403 on /) exposes a reachable stage/path (e.g. /prod, /v1, /api) returning backend content or a different error class
hypotheses.attacker_view: enumerate gateway stages to reach undocumented QA API operations
hypotheses.defender_view: gateway has no deployed stages or all stages require auth; 403 on every path

hypotheses.statement: The rejection may be channel-specific; the same assumption may fail on a sibling endpoint.
hypotheses.investigator_test: Map sibling endpoints sharing the object and test the cheapest one.

hypotheses.statement: beta.api.login.yahoo.com (older/secondary API version) validates requests more weakly than api.login.yahoo.com — e.g. different auth requirements, verbose errors, or missing rate limits on the same endpoints
hypotheses.attacker_view: find an endpoint that is locked on prod API but open/verbose on the beta API version
hypotheses.defender_view: both API versions share the same validation and auth enforcement

hypotheses.statement: Ownership is enforced on GET but not re-checked on state-changing verbs.
hypotheses.investigator_test: Replay the same object access via PATCH/PUT/DELETE as non-owner; diff against GET.

hypotheses.statement: Ownership is enforced at the controller but skipped on a nested/member route.
hypotheses.investigator_test: Reach the same object through nested routes (/parent/:id/child) and member actions.

hypotheses.statement: api.stage.screenname.aol.com enforces auth per-method: GET returns 401 but POST/PUT/DELETE/OPTIONS receive different handling (200/405/500), indicating method-based auth bypass or verbose method exposure
hypotheses.attacker_view: use POST/PUT against screenname API operations that only guard GET
hypotheses.defender_view: ATS enforces auth uniformly across methods; all non-GET return 401/405 uniformly

hypotheses.statement: login.yahoo.com/oauth2/request_auth does not strictly validate redirect_uri against the client registration, allowing an attacker to receive authorization codes at an evil domain
hypotheses.attacker_view: craft authorize URL with victim client_id but evil redirect_uri; victim approves; code goes to attacker
hypotheses.defender_view: Yahoo enforces exact redirect_uri match per OAuth 2.0; mismatches show an error, never redirect

spec.expected_observation: response contains Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://evil.example.com AND Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
spec.reason: CORS misconfig is a classic logic flaw on large estates; Yahoo's estate includes hundreds of legacy API hosts where allowlist may be loose. Single GET with Origin header is the minimal discriminating test.
spec.auth_basis: HackerOne public program: automated tools permitted at reasonable rates against in-scope assets; single manual-style request per host, no DoS, no user data
spec.success_criteria: ACAO echoes our origin AND ACAC is true on an endpoint that serves user-influenced data
spec.failure_criteria: ACAO absent, or echoes only whitelisted origins, or ACAC not true

warnings: no evidence either way: low prior, keep the experiment minimal

answers.benign_explanation: Yahoo uses a strict allowlist of origins on API endpoints; main properties hardened

spec.auth_basis: HackerOne public program (*.techcrunch.com in scope): read-only GET requests, no auth bypass, no brute force, no DoS
spec.failure_criteria: 401/403/empty on REST endpoint AND no author redirect

spec.expected_observation: identical GET / to both hosts returns DIFFERENT status/body/headers (e.g. beta returns 200/verbose where prod returns 401, or beta leaks stack traces)
spec.reason: API version gaps are a classic logic flaw; Yahoo runs parallel api.login and beta.api.login hosts. A differential GET on / is the minimal test — one request per host, same headers, compare.
spec.auth_basis: HackerOne public program: 2 read-only GETs to in-scope API hosts, no auth bypass, no DoS
spec.success_criteria: material difference in status/body/headers indicating weaker validation on beta
spec.failure_criteria: identical 401/headers on both (no version gap on /)

spec.reason: Parallel API deployments (prod vs beta) frequently drift in auth enforcement. Comparing the two login API roots with identical requests isolates version as the single variable.

spec.reason: redirect_uri validation is the linchpin of OAuth code flow; a single authorize request with a dummy client_id and evil redirect_uri discriminates. No credentials, no user session, no code redemption — validation behavior only.

results.observed: /wp-json/ -> 302 to wp-login.php; /wp-json/wp/v2/users -> 302 to login; /?author=1 -> 302 to wp-login.php?redirect_to; xmlrpc.php -> connection refused (000); no generator meta. No username disclosed anywhere without auth.
results.why_failed: dev WP instance forces login for all WP routes including REST API; xmlrpc dead at network edge
results.learned: develop.techcrunch.com is a hardened WP: auth wall on every route. Do not spend more time on WP user-enum here. Pivot to API-gateway host and OAuth surfaces.

results.observed: GET /prod, /v1, /api on api.qa.cmi.aol.com all return 403 {"message":"Forbidden"} — identical to /. No deployed stage reachable. (Note: mid-test sandbox egress outage caused transient 000s; retried after recovery with 12s spacing.)
results.why_failed: API Gateway has no reachable stages under common names; 403 uniform across / and stage paths
results.learned: api.qa.cmi.aol.com is a locked-down API Gateway. Stage-guessing beyond 3 common names is noisy — stop here.

results.observed: GET query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/AAPL with evil Origin returned 429 Too Many Requests (no CORS headers in 429). Edge is rate-limiting this egress IP after earlier sweeps.
results.learned: Yahoo edge 429s this IP — back off Yahoo hosts for 30+ min; pivot to aol.com/techcrunch.com infra which is separate. CORS on finance API untested, not rejected.

results.observed: GET / on api.login.yahoo.com and beta.api.login.yahoo.com both return 401 Unauthorized, Server ATS, identical 12-byte body. No version skew on root path.
results.why_failed: both API versions enforce auth identically on /
results.learned: login API prod/beta are in sync on /. Version-gap testing needs deeper known endpoints, not root.

results.observed: POST to api.stage.screenname.aol.com timed out (000); follow-up GET also 000. Host was 401 at 19:42 UTC. Egress confirmed working (example.com 200, www.aol.com 200) — this is per-host throttling/flakiness, not IP block.
results.learned: api.stage.screenname.aol.com throttles after a few requests. Method-differential untested, not rejected. Cool down this host; use fresh hosts.
